match.reason: The bank point covers inventory management, holding costs and FIFO/LIFO valuation for Year 12 Business Studies, which is broader and at a different depth than the new point's basic definition of inventory as a trading business's current asset.

draft.title: What inventory is
card: Inventory is the goods a trading business buys so that it can sell them for a profit. It is also called stock.
Inventory is a current asset, because the business expects to sell it within the next 12 months.
Items used to run the business, such as a shop's shelves or a delivery van, are not inventory. The business keeps them and does not plan to sell them.
For most trading businesses, inventory is the largest current asset on the balance sheet. It is usually worth more than the cash or accounts receivable the business holds.
draft.remember: Inventory is what a trading business holds to resell, and it is usually its largest current asset.

a.q: Which item is inventory for a bicycle shop run by Priya in Ballarat?
opts: Bicycles bought from a supplier to sell to customers
The shelving the bicycles are displayed on
The cash register used at the counter
The van used to collect goods from suppliers
a.why: The bicycles were bought to be resold for a profit, so they are inventory. The shelving, cash register and van are used to run the shop and are not meant to be sold.
a.clue: Which item is bought in order to be sold on?

b.q: Tom owns a hardware store in Geelong. He buys a new computer to record sales, and he buys 200 hammers from a supplier. Which statement is correct?
opts: The hammers are inventory and the computer is not
The computer is inventory and the hammers are not
Both are inventory, as both were bought for the store
Neither is inventory, as both were bought on credit
b.why: The hammers were bought to be resold, so they are inventory. The computer is used to run the store and Tom does not plan to sell it. Buying something for the business does not make it inventory, and paying on credit does not change that.
b.clue: Ask what the business plans to do with each item.

a.best: Bicycles bought from a supplier to sell to customers

b.best: The hammers are inventory and the computer is not
